title: Testing Equivalent Expressions with Desmos Sliders
description: Compare expressions at the same distinct allowed slider values, eliminate choices that mismatch, and retest ties while recognizing that numerical matches do not prove an identity.

questions.stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \((2x+3y)(4x-5y)\) for all real x and y?
questions.explanation_html: Use the same nonzero values for both variables to eliminate mismatches. The cross-products combine to 2xy, and expansion gives \(8x^2+2xy-15y^2\) for all inputs.
questions.variation: Compare two products with both sliders set

distractor_notes.B: Adds the cross terms without keeping the negative sign.
distractor_notes.D: Loses the negative sign in the product of the y terms.

questions.stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \((2x-5y)^2\) for all real x and y?
questions.explanation_html: Try two nonzero slider values. Choices that omit or change a cross term fail for suitable values. Expansion confirms the exact identity \(4x^2-20xy+25y^2\).
questions.variation: Use nonzero values to distinguish square expansions

distractor_notes.C: Uses the expansion of the sum.

questions.stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \(5(x+2y)-3(x-4y)\) for all real x and y?
questions.explanation_html: Set both sliders to nonzero values and use a second pair if needed. Distributing each factor gives an x coefficient of 2 and a y coefficient of 22.
questions.variation: Retest after distributing a negative across grouped terms

distractor_notes.A: Does not distribute the subtraction across the second y term.
distractor_notes.D: Does not scale the y terms.

questions.stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \((2x^2y)^2(3xy^4)\) for all real x and y?
questions.explanation_html: Choose legal inputs apart from 0 or 1 to detect changed powers. Squaring the first factor and multiplying yields \(12x^5y^{6}\).
questions.variation: Choose nontrivial values that expose changes in powers

distractor_notes.A: Does not square the first coefficient.
distractor_notes.D: Does not square y in the first factor.

questions.stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{2x^2-18y^2}{x-3y}\) for all real x and y with \(x\ne 3y\)?
questions.explanation_html: Use slider values with x different from 3y. The numerator factors as 2 times the product of x − 3y and x + 3y, so the quotient is \(2x+6y\).
questions.variation: Test an equivalent quotient using allowed slider values

distractor_notes.C: Drops the scale of the numerator.
distractor_notes.D: Uses the squared factor in the remaining linear term.
